---
title: "Show a table and a chart in a notebook"
jupyter: php
---

Read a CSV file into a phibble data frame, summarize it in one notebook cell,
and plot it in the next.

Requires the `php` kernel from [Installation](../install.qmd). The pipe tab
needs PHP 8.5, and the method chain runs on PHP 8.3 and later.

## Setup

Create a Composer project and start JupyterLab in it:

```bash
mkdir mtcars && cd mtcars
composer require phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr \
    phpstats/phiz
~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab
```

Create a notebook with the PHP kernel from the launcher. The data is
[mtcars](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#mtcars) from R's `datasets`
package: fuel economy (`mpg`, miles per gallon), cylinders (`cyl`), weight
(`wt`, in 1,000 lb), and other design measures of 32 cars tested by *Motor
Trend* in 1974. The notebook reads it from the phpstats datasets repository by
URL.

## Cells

- A `use` statement applies to its own cell and every later one.
- phplyr's `round()` replaces PHP's built-in `round()` in the cells after the
  import.

```{php}
use Phibble\DataFrame;
use Phiz\Plot;
use function Phplyr\{phplyr, group_by, summarize};
use function Phplyr\{arrange, desc, n, mean, round};
```

A cell's last value is its output. A phibble data frame is shown as a table.
The summary counts the cars with each number of cylinders and averages their
fuel economy.

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}

## PHP 8.5+

```{php}
$mtcars = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/'
    .'phpstats/datasets/main/csv/mtcars.csv'
);

$mtcars |>
    group_by('cyl') |>
    summarize(cars: n(), mpg: round(mean('mpg'), 1)) |>
    arrange(desc('mpg'));
```

## PHP 8.3–8.4

```{php}
$mtcars = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/'
    .'phpstats/datasets/main/csv/mtcars.csv'
);

phplyr($mtcars)
    ->groupBy('cyl')
    ->summarize(cars: n(), mpg: round(mean('mpg'), 1))
    ->arrange(desc('mpg'))
    ->get();
```

:::

Variables persist across cells, so the next cell plots `$mtcars` from the cell
before. A phiz plot is shown as a chart, here fuel economy against weight.

```{php}
Plot::of($mtcars)
    ->aes(x: 'wt', y: 'mpg')
    ->point()
    ->labs(x: 'Weight (1,000 lb)', y: 'Miles per gallon');
```

See also: [Rich output](../get-started.qmd#rich-output),
[JupyterLab](../jupyter.qmd), [phplyr](https://phplyr.phpstats.org), and
[phiz](https://phiz.phpstats.org).
